vulnerabilities.description: Session files created with default permissions (644), allowing other users on the system to read sensitive context data. Use fs.writeFileSync with mode 0o600 to restrict to owner only.
Memory files created with default permissions (644). Sensitive data stored in plain text JSON without encryption. Should use restrictive file permissions (0o600) and consider encrypting values.
Session context can store arbitrary sensitive data (API keys, tokens) in plain text. No encryption applied. Context should be sanitized or encrypted before storage.
No access control or authorization checks. Any process on the system can call session.update() to modify session data maliciously.
No input validation on memory keys/values. Missing authorization checks. Any process can set arbitrary data including malicious payloads.
Temporary files created with default permissions (likely 644). On multi-user systems, temp file contents (GitHub bodies) could be world-readable before cleanup. Use mode 0o600.
Silent error handling when loading memory file. Errors are caught but ignored, potentially masking data corruption or access issues.
RegExp created from user input via process.argv without escaping. If task input is untrusted, ReDoS attacks possible, though impact is limited to DoS within router.
Non-atomic read-modify-write in session.update(). Concurrent access could cause data loss if multiple processes modify sessions simultaneously.

recommendations: Set restrictive file permissions (0o600) when creating session.json, memory.json, and temp files. Use fs.writeFileSync(path, data, {mode: 0o600}) or fs.chmodSync() after creation.
Encrypt sensitive context data at rest. Consider using crypto module to encrypt/decrypt session context values before storage.
Add input validation to memory.js set/delete operations. Reject suspicious keys (e.g., containing path traversal patterns like '../').
Implement basic access control by storing user/process info with session data and validating on read/write operations.
Replace silent error catches. Log meaningful errors to stderr for debugging while still handling gracefully.
Use fs.promises and implement atomic file operations or file locking for concurrent access safety.
Sanitize user input in router.js by escaping RegExp special characters: `task.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&')`
No hardcoded secrets found (✓) but document secure credential handling in code comments.
No SQL injection, XSS, or dependency vulnerabilities detected in provided code, though full npm audit recommended.
